stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model benefits from Ollama's MLX engine, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is implementing new restrictions on 'full disk access' for macOS.
The change is a direct response to security risks introduced by increasingly capable AI agents.
The new controls aim to ensure users intentionally grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A tech CEO was arrested for allegedly smuggling $300M worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent challenges regarding export controls and chip smuggling.
This case underscores the geopolitical tensions surrounding advanced semiconductor technology.

stories.title: OpenAI and Cerebras Confirm 750MW AI Inference Deployment Through 2028
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI and Cerebras have formalized a major partnership.
The deployment involves a massive scale of 750MW of Cerebras wafer-scale computing.
The commitment spans multiple years, extending through 2028, signaling long-term infrastructure investment in AI inference.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary application in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking of major LLMs.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured $88 million in funding from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
The company boasts a significant user base, serving 8.9 million developers.
The news highlights the growing commercial and developer adoption of open-source AI models.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speedup is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% performance improvement according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in animating 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to replace heavy per-frame neural decoding.
Demonstrates that avatar animation can be effectively approximated using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Emphasizes the importance of accurate command syntax in cybersecurity, where minor errors can lead to operational failures.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that approximates complex neural decoding using linear combinations of blendshapes.
Significantly improves real-time performance by replacing per-frame heavy neural decoding with a shallow coefficient predictor.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a novel method to systematically probe and diagnose LLM capabilities in mathematics.
The findings aim to provide a framework for improving LLMs through targeted post-training based on diagnosed mathematical weaknesses.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for making typed decisions.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers regarding yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows users to build custom hardware gadgets featuring the Muse AI.
Suggested applications include displaying reminders on E Ink screens or running Muse on HDMI sticks.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly changing its content strategy, moving away from high-budget, prestige productions.
This shift is evidenced by the termination or winding down of multiyear production deals with established directors.
The change signals a potential strategic pivot in how Netflix invests in and acquires content compared to its past model.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced a new agent platform named Dots.
Dots is positioned as enterprise software, capable of performing tasks like ordering food.
The platform is contrasted with competitors like Meta Muse, suggesting a more 'workplace' focus.

stories.title: Rivian’s sales pop as the company’s big R2 bet starts to pay off
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Rivian reported a significant increase in Q3 production and deliveries.
Production rose by 85% year-over-year, while deliveries jumped 45%.
The positive sales trend is linked to the anticipated success of the more affordable R2 vehicle.

stories.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: OpenAI has released 'Dots,' a new product positioned as a business-focused alternative to Muse.
Dots is a paid service, starting at a minimum of $100 per month.
The product appears to offer similar creative capabilities to Muse but with a business-centric focus.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon has a $1 billion initiative aimed at addressing public concerns regarding its data centers.
The company received mixed reactions, being praised for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
However, the plan faced criticism for allegedly downplaying the environmental impact and pollution from its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a significant lawsuit regarding the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
The resolution faces criticism from groups claiming drivers are still owed more.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous self-improvement of embodied robot agents.
The system improves robot execution capabilities without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
RPG uses offline datasets to identify manipulation skills and generates simulation tasks for practice using execution feedback.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to find inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, where researchers annotate which past works influenced their own projects.
This addresses a key gap in current AI research: the ability to synthesize and discover novel connections within vast scientific literature.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations of current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
Uses compact sliding-window slice latents to represent shapes, aiming for topology-preserving generation.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock reasoning potential in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities.
The system maintains a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve past environmental observations.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independence bottleneck in discrete models, where tokens are sampled separately, losing statistical dependencies.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which allows for better modeling of inter-token relationships.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) for faster visual generation.
DMAD reframes distribution matching as a classification task to learn log-density ratios directly.
It aims to overcome the high memory and computational costs associated with auxiliary diffusion models in previous methods.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR aims to explicitly encode complex chemical structures like ring systems and recurring motifs, which standard formalisms struggle with.
The framework is designed to be topology-aware while overcoming the computational demands and decoding difficulties of existing higher-order representations.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings instead of fixed class labels or text prompts as conditioning in diffusion transformers.
The method, named Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), trains a Transformer to predict the subsequent continuous embedding in a sequence.
This approach leverages the inherent structure of image generation where the clean image's embeddings follow the noisy image's embeddings.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) regarding surface fragmentation and topological inconsistency.
Uses compact sliding-window slice latents to represent shapes while preserving topology.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO is a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The optimizer addresses the memory bottleneck caused by large optimizer states, which currently limits model size deployment on GPUs.
TACO aims to improve upon existing methods (like Muon) by offering a sparse, column-wise update mechanism while maintaining a geometry closer to standard AdamW.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are proposed as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Discrete diffusion models suffer from a bottleneck where parallel decoding samples tokens independently, losing statistical dependencies.
CDLMs address this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token dependencies during generation.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning optimization.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size determination.
Uses a trusted first-order optimizer for direction, followed by zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size selection.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: KaliBench introduces a fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
It addresses a critical gap in current evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
The benchmark incorporates runtime-free verifiable rewards, focusing on the syntactic correctness and utility of the generated commands.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to find inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark is built using expert annotations from researchers who identify which past works influenced their own projects.
This work addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, buried ideas within vast scientific archives.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models overcome this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token dependencies.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage context in long-horizon software engineering tasks.
Addresses the challenge of stale context in agents performing complex, multi-step coding tasks (inspection, search, editing).
The agent learns when and how to compact its working state to maintain efficiency without losing critical information.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper proposes a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to rigorously test and validate tool-use claims in smaller models.
The study demonstrates false positives using matched Spanish security language models, highlighting the limitations of lenient evaluation metrics.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new finetuning technique using sampling to improve frontier models.
It challenges the conventional view that Reinforcement Learning (RL) is superior to Supervised Finetuning (SFT) for generalization.
The research explores the trade-offs between SFT's ability to use off-policy data and RL's generalization strengths.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to test data agents on complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces Where-OPD, a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by supervising student models using a privileged, frozen version of themselves.
It addresses a gap in current MLLM research, which often limits visual information use to simple image crops for perception tasks.

stories.title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI until now
stories.author: PaulHoule
bullet_points: AI models have recently succeeded in playing the game Stratego, a game characterized by hidden information.
The research suggests that the complexity of hidden information presented a significant challenge to previous AI attempts.
The findings are supported by publications in Nature and arXiv, indicating academic rigor in the development.

stories.title: The Four Horsemen of Agentic Coding
stories.author: distantprovince.substack.com via guillego
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Agentic Coding,' a growing trend in AI software development.
It frames the key components or challenges of this paradigm as the 'Four Horsemen.'
The topic is highly relevant to modern software engineering and advanced AI applications.

stories.title: Building Sarrera: Self-Hosted Enterprise AI Inference Gateway with RBAC, Token Quotas & Telemetry
stories.author: marioezquerro
bullet_points: Details the architecture for a self-hosted, private AI inference gateway.
Integrates key components like LiteLLM, Caddy, Langfuse, and Open WebUI.
Focuses on enterprise features such as Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and token quotas.
